dct_description_sm: Bean goose currently nest almost exclusively in Finnmark. It has an uncertain conservation status among breeding birds in Norway, and the level of knowledge about the influencing factors are sparse. Bean goose assumed to have declined dramatically in recent decades, and particularly considering fabalis fabalis, with an estimated world population of about 60,000 individuals. In order to improve our knowledge NOF has a project to capture bean geese and mark them with color-coded neck rings on Valdak Marshes in Porsanger, but also on the Varanger Peninsula in Finnmark. A small number of birds have also been fitted with satellite radio transmitters. This can give us answers on how the Norwegian geese prefer and where they spend the winter, and they overwinter separately from Swedish / Finnish populations. In the long term it can also give us an overview of demographic factors such as survival of adults and young birds. Management measures can be implemented using this information to ensure that the Bean Goose does not disappear from the Norway.
dct_title_s: Monitoring of Bean Goose in Finnmark, Norway
